A1.justification: Both PDFs contain the same ASAP research work, with complete main text, six figures, ten tables, and supplementary Sections 6–7. Text extraction and visual inspection support comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original DGM4 detection and grounding results, component ablations, and supplementary modality, large-model, and hyperparameter experiments.

after.justification: v2 retains the original DGM4 results and the main-text and supplementary experimental analyses in Tables 1–10.

M1.justification: LMA, MGCA, PMM, hard-negative patch selection, training objectives, and inference remain unchanged. Section 6.3 corrects its classifier description to match the existing equation rather than introducing a different method.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same DGM4 dataset and four detection, classification, and grounding tasks. The Table 5 heading revision does not introduce additional dataset or task coverage.

E2.justification: Table 1 retains CLIP, VILT, HAMMER, HAMMER++, VIKI, and UFAFormer. Comparator membership also remains unchanged throughout the ablations and supplementary large-model comparisons.

E3.justification: The evaluation metrics, image preprocessing, model configurations, batch size of 32, 50 training epochs, optimization schedule, and hyperparameter sweeps remain unchanged. No new evaluation procedure is reported.

E4.justification: Tables 2–10 retain the same component, auxiliary-text, negative-selection, modality, large-model, and hyperparameter analyses. Figure 5 retains the same attention visualizations and qualitative examples.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, error bars, or formal significance tests. Statistical uncertainty reporting is unchanged.

E6.justification: Table 1 revises the average improvement over HAMMER: HAMMER++ changes from +0.42 to +0.39, VIKI from +0.57 to +0.37, UFAFormer from +1.12 to +1.13, and ASAP from +2.54 to +2.40. All underlying task scores and other experimental results remain unchanged. Section 4.3 still states ASAP's average improvement as 2.54.

T1.justification: Equations 1–13 and the supplementary loss formulas are unchanged. Section 6.3 replaces C_b with C_m in its prose, matching the already existing equation; this does not revise the mathematical formulation.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same semantic-alignment motivation, LMA and MGCA contributions, and claims of improved manipulation detection and grounding.

C2.justification: The interpretations of component effects, attention behavior, multimodal fusion, large-model selection, and hyperparameter results remain unchanged. No substantive limitations or applicability qualifications are added.

D1.justification: Hardware, backbones, auxiliary models, prompts, implementation settings, and hyperparameters remain unchanged. Both versions promise code release at the same repository; no changed access or reproducibility information is provided.

R1.justification: The 30-entry bibliography and related-work discussion remain unchanged, but v2 adds three unresolved citation groups in the introduction. They visibly render as question marks, so the supplied PDFs do not establish which works, if any, were newly cited.

P1.justification: v2 adds acknowledgments and corresponding-author information and revises the task and classifier wording in Section 6.3. The main narrative and section organization otherwise remain substantially unchanged.

P2.justification: Figure 2 has small graphical and legend refinements. Table 5 changes its heading from Image Grounding to Text Grounding, and Table 1 adds ASAP's publication venue. There is minor page reflow, with all figures and tables retained.

improvement.justification: The revised Table 1 averages better match the retained scores, and the appendix wording and heading edits improve clarity. However, v2 introduces unresolved citations and leaves Section 4.3's 2.54 claim inconsistent with Table 1's 2.40. With the scientific method and experimental evidence otherwise unchanged, these limited benefits and new reporting defects do not establish a clear net quality improvement or deterioration.
